key_insight: AI-driven landscape design education should teach an evidence-constrained design process, not just AI tool operation.
engineering_relevance: The framework links reusable research and design precedents with site-specific AI analysis and generation to guide context-sensitive design decisions.
method: Combine research findings, design precedents, AI-based recognition and judgment, and AI generation.
Organize student work into reading the site, grounding the context, and giving form.
Guide each stage with evidence, complementary elements, partial embedding, and explicit judgment.
evidence_signal: The framework draws on 114 retrievable situation packages distilled from 13 street design guidelines and is illustrated through three classroom examples, without learning-outcome data.
watch_item: Its effectiveness in improving student learning or design quality remains unvalidated.
paper_title: AI-DRIVEN, EVIDENCE-BASED GENERATIVE DESIGN: A TEACHING FRAMEWORK FOR LANDSCAPE ARCHITECTONICS INTEGRATING RESEARCH FINDINGS, DESIGN PRECEDENTS, AND INTELLIGENT RECOGNITION AND JUDGMENT
